subject: physics
question_text: Derive the equations for the kinetic energy and the potential energy of a simple harmonic oscillator, and show that the total energy of a particle in simple harmonic motion is constant at any point on its path.

verification.note: The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Kinetic energy
lines: A particle of mass m in SHM has displacement
so its velocity is v = A ω cos ωt, which can
be written in terms of y as

lines.text: KE = ½ m v² = ½ m ω² (A² − y²)

steps.why: Writing v in terms of y rather than t is the key move — it lets KE and PE be added at the SAME position later.
common_mistakes: Leaving v as A ω cos ωt, so KE and PE end up in different variables and cannot be added.

recall.must_convey: That v is omega root A squared minus y squared, so KE is half m omega squared into A squared minus y squared.
accept: v is omega root A squared minus y squared
KE is half m omega squared A squared minus y squared
reject: PE is half m omega squared y squared

steps.memory_tip: Write v in terms of y, not t: v = ω√(A² − y²), so KE = ½mω²(A² − y²).

steps.label: Potential energy
lines: At a displacement y the restoring force is
F = −m ω² y. The work done AGAINST it in
moving a further small distance dy is
Integrating from 0 to y, this work is stored
in the particle as potential energy:
steps.why: The force is not constant, so the work has to be integrated — using F × y directly would give twice the right answer.
common_mistakes: Writing PE = m ω² y² by multiplying force and distance without integrating.

recall.must_convey: That the work done against the restoring force integrates to PE equal to half m omega squared y squared.
accept: integrate m omega squared y dy
PE is half m omega squared y squared
reject: KE is half m omega squared A squared minus y squared

steps.memory_tip: The force grows with y, so integrate — PE = ½mω²y². Using F × y directly gives twice the answer.

steps.label: At the three positions

lines.text: KE = ½ m ω² A²,    PE = 0
KE = 0,    PE = ½ m ω² A²

lines: At any position y, both are non-zero:

lines.text: KE = ½ m ω²(A² − y²),  PE = ½ m ω² y²

steps.why: The energy simply moves back and forth between the two forms — fastest at the middle, still at the ends.
common_mistakes: Saying the kinetic energy is zero at the mean position; that is where it is largest.

recall.must_convey: That KE is maximum and PE zero at the mean position, and the reverse at the extremes.
accept: KE maximum at the mean position
reject: integrate m omega squared y dy

steps.memory_tip: Three positions to quote: mean (all kinetic), extreme (all potential), in between (shared).

steps.label: The graph
steps.why: The two curves are mirror parabolas, and the flat line on top is the statement being proved: their sum never changes.
common_mistakes: Drawing the total-energy line sloping instead of flat.

recall.must_convey: That KE and PE are drawn as opposite parabolas against y, with their sum a flat line.
accept: draw the KE and PE parabolas
reject: E is half m omega squared A squared

steps.memory_tip: Two mirror parabolas and one flat line on top — the flat line is the total energy.

steps.label: Total energy
lines: Adding the two at any position y, the y² terms

lines.text: E = KE + PE = ½ m ω² A²

lines: The total energy is the same at every point of
the path. It depends only on m, ω and A, and
not on where the particle happens to be.
steps.why: The cancellation of y² IS the proof — the position drops out, which is what "constant at any point on its path" means.
common_mistakes: Checking only the mean and extreme positions and calling that a proof for every point.

recall.must_convey: That the y squared terms cancel, giving total energy half m omega squared A squared everywhere.
accept: E is half m omega squared A squared
reject: draw the KE and PE parabolas

steps.memory_tip: Add KE and PE: the y² terms cancel. That cancellation IS the proof.

insider_note: The graph carries its own mark: two mirror curves and the flat total line.
